To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the design and synthesis of a novel class of potent Gram-negative only LpxC inhibitors was completed.

(i) the 2-aminopyridine hydroxamic acid scaffold was identified as a potent LpxC inhibitor with antibacterial activity; (ii) the 2-amino-4-alkylpyridine hydroxamates are potent and selective inhibitors of LpxC and are active against Gram-negative bacteria; and (iii) the 2-pyridone and 2-pyrimidone hydroxamates have potent LpxC inhibitory activity and
we have identified novel potent and selective LpxC inhibitors with antibacterial activity that are Gram-negative specific.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and synthesis of novel Gram-negative specific LpsC inhibitors.
the discovery of potent and specific Gram-negative LpxC inhibitors as novel antibiotics.
the design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of novel LpxC inhibitors with the ultimate aim of identifying new antibiotics for Gram-negative bacterial infections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the design, synthesis and biological testing of a series of novel LpxC inhibitors has been completed.
the design and synthesis of novel Gram-negative specific LPS biosynthesis inhibitors is a viable approach to developing new antibiotics.
the chemistry effort has led to the discovery and optimization of novel Gram-negative specific LPS biosynthesis inhibitors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the hydroxamic acid moiety can be replaced with a variety of functional groups that are capable of coordinating the enzyme's catalytically essential zinc ion and that the resulting compounds retain potent antibacterial activity.

we have identified novel inhibitors of LpxC that have improved antibacterial properties compared to CHIR-909, a compound with potent antibacterial activity against Gram-negative bacteria and no activity against Gram-positive bacteria.
we have identified a novel class of potent Gram-negative LpxC inhibitors and that we have demonstrated their potential to be developed into a new antibacterial drug class.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 4-hydroxybenzoic acid hydroxamic acid warhead is a viable alternative to the 4-heteroarylbenzene hydroxamate warheads.
the 4-hydroxamic acid is a viable warhead for Gram-negative specific LPS inhibitors.

a small change in the hydroxamate zinc-binding warhead of LpxC inhibitors can result in dramatic changes in potency, which is an important observation that will be useful for future medicinal chemistry efforts.
